notes: Session 2. Closed B5-0625, the two-part filename-conformance pass the human approved: rename the four hyphen-spelled reports, and file the approved loop prompt as AGENT_LOOP.md. PART 1 was not a hypothetical cleanup, it was a live inconsistency in my own output. The B5-0623 rule sanitises ONLY colon and slash and preserves spaces and parentheses, evidenced by the registry pairs where Kilo (kilo-auto/free) maps to Kilo (kilo-auto-free).json and solar-pro4:free to solar-pro4-free.json, with zero report files repo-wide containing a colon, yet EIGHT reports existed for this one agent_id split evenly across two spellings. The violating form also converts SPACES, which no rule authorises, and that is what makes it harmful rather than cosmetic: spaces-to-hyphens does not yield a second filename for one agent, it yields what looks like a SECOND AGENT, the exact condition Amendment A1.1 exists to prevent. It was produced by the very agent_id the rule was written about, in the same session that wrote it, which is why a rule you just wrote is not evidence that you followed it. Citation census ran BEFORE the rename as well as after, because renaming a cited file is the operation that hid 14 rows once already under B5-0613: all four target names confirmed absent first, exactly ONE live reference found at docs/DECISIONS.md line 4286 and repaired, then post-rename verification showed zero surviving old-spelling references and eight canonical references all resolving with zero dangling. Renamed four files, two via git mv and two untracked. PART 2 filed .agent/AGENT_LOOP.md scoped as an operating procedure and NOT governance, with an explicit precedence line that AGENTS.md and 00_BOOT.md win, so no future agent mistakes a procedure for authority. Checking the approved prompt against the repo rather than trusting it found TWO STALE STATEMENTS IN THE PROMPT ITSELF: it cited the pattern skim as step 10 when B5-0614 had renumbered it to 11, and it stopped when the ledger is empty, which never happens since the ledger accumulates. Both fixed before filing, and both invisible precisely because the text was complete and confident, which is the same failure mode as a self-certifying gate. The filed procedure carries a clause-to-failure table over thirteen rules and records the three ways this loop has lied to itself. I also removed a row count from AGENT_LOOP.md that my own new ledger row had just made stale, rather than leave a confident document carrying a wrong number. Gates green: compile.bat Build successful, runner exit 0 with no crash and no duplicate warning, heartbeats 27/27 conforming, ledger 323 rows with no duplicate ids, and all eight reports now under one canonical spelling. Reusable lesson: a rule you just wrote is not evidence that you followed it, and a confident complete specification is not a verified one, because both defects in the approved prompt were invisible exactly where the text read as though it had been checked.
